context:
Start with API classification and small ambiguity removals. Treat a
benchmark-family plugin seam as a design gate before extraction, and use tests
to keep wrappers, registries, and loaders aligned.
description:
Benchmark APIs are split across tested top-level wrappers, a public
benchbox.base.BaseBenchmark, a small remaining core.base_benchmark class,
lazy registries, loaders, and benchmark-family code inside broad core/base
mixins. The wrappers are not accidental; tests assert facade behavior. The
cleanup target is the remaining ambiguous base/loader split and the lack of a
benchmark-family extension boundary, not a wrapper purge.

This item classifies benchmark API surfaces, retires or justifies the second
base class, and prepares a benchmark-family plugin seam without a broad
rewrite.

anti_patterns.dont: create a third benchmark base class while cleaning up two existing bases
anti_patterns.why: remove, alias, or justify the secondary base.

anti_patterns.dont: interpret duplicate wrapper reachability as accidental
split core by moving files mechanically
anti_patterns.why: dependency direction and public API status must drive the boundary.

deferrals.reason: Large structural refactor should follow the public API decision and plugin-seam ADR.
deferrals.summary: Split all of benchbox/core into engine and benchmark packages

deferrals.reason: Wrappers are tested as public facades unless explicitly deprecated.
deferrals.resolved_reason: [G4 sweep] non-actionable: Reason explicitly rejects removal: wrapper facades are tested public surfaces unless explicitly deprecated.

preserves.behavior: Do not break top-level wrapper facade tests unless an explicit deprecation path lands in the same PR.
Do not introduce platform adapter imports into core engine modules.
Do not move benchmark-family code in a way that changes result bundle shape.

prior_art.concept: docs/development/run-lifecycle-map.md: existing lifecycle documentation -- align any plugin seam with this flow.
docs/reference/backward-compatibility.md: existing base-class lifecycle entries -- update rather than invent separate lifecycle docs.
tests/unit/test_wrapper_facades_fast.py: existing wrapper contract tests -- preserve as public API evidence.

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/unit/test_wrapper_facades_fast.py tests -k 'benchmark_loader or base_benchmark' --tb=short
verifications.description: Run wrapper facade and benchmark loader tests.

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests -k 'import_boundary or core_boundary' --tb=short
verifications.description: Run import-boundary check added by this item.
verifications.expected: Core/platform dependency boundary tests pass or known exemptions are documented.

work_units.notes:
Added docs/design/future-state/benchmark-family-plugin-seam/README.md and
linked it from the future-state index. The design keeps wrappers and
result bundles stable, defines family-owned versus shared-runtime
responsibilities, and requires one pilot family before any broad package
extraction.
work_units.summary: Design the benchmark-family plugin seam as an ADR before extraction

work_units.notes:
Added a narrow AST import-boundary check over benchbox/base.py,
benchbox/core/base_benchmark.py, benchbox/core/benchmark_loader.py,
benchbox/core/__init__.py, and benchbox/core/tuning/. The check forbids
concrete benchbox.platforms imports in those benchmark API and tuning
boundary files while avoiding unrelated existing core/platform couplings.
work_units.summary: Add an import-boundary check for core modules that depend on platform adapters
